title: kernel-latency-variance-decomposition-notes
body:
Summary:

This note records an exploratory investigation into high tail latency variance we observed for attention kernels during inference runs. The goal is to decompose the sources of spikes (p99/p999) across FlashAttention, paged-attention, and fused ops kernels and to capture reproducible profiling steps and mitigations. The investigation focuses on long sequence and mixed sequence workloads where variance is most visible.

High-level observations:
- Stable p50 in most cases; p99 shows large, inconsistent spikes (2-4x median) for certain sequence length / batch size combos.
- Spikes correlate with: occasional device-host memory activity, CUDA kernel launch stalls, and intermittent CPU-side stalls (Python GIL/GC in our harness).
- Fused ops variant tends to have lower average latency and tighter p99 for single-stream, low-batch setups; FlashAttention is best for medium batches/seq lengths but shows rare long-running kernel invocations in some configurations. Paged-attention reduces peak memory usage but sometimes increases variance due to async page faults and prefetch races.

Test platform and harness:
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100-SXM 80GB (multi-instance tests), also reproduces on A10 and A40.
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04, NVIDIA driver 535.x, CUDA 12.1, cuDNN 9.x
- Runtime: pytorch 2.2, custom runtime v0.19.3 (serving-runtime branch kernel-variance), kernels compiled with fatbin and autotune flags enabled.
- Harness: lightweight HTTP microbench (go client) sending steady request streams; runner pinned to a single NUMA domain for deterministic CPU affinity.

Profiling commands used (repro steps):
1) System-level trace (nsys):
   nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output=nsys_run_01 python ./bench/harness.py --workload attention_variance --config configs/seq2048_b1.json

2) Torch profiler snippet (collection around hot region):
   import torch
   from torch.profiler import profile, record_function, ProfilerActivity
   with profile(activities=[ProfilerActivity.CPU, ProfilerActivity.CUDA], record_shapes=True, with_stack=False) as prof:
       with record_function("attention_forward"):
           model.forward(batch)
   print(prof.key_averages().table(sort_by="cuda_time_total", row_limit=20))

3) Kernel-level sampling (nsight-cli + nvtx markers): use NVTX to bracket attention kernels and look at overlapping memcpy and kernel launches.

Representative microbench results (selected cells, aggregated across 50 warm runs + 200 measured runs):

Table: seq_len x batch combinations (A100, single model replica)

seq_len=512, batch=8:
- FlashAttention: p50=18ms, p90=25ms, p99=38ms
- PagedAttention: p50=22ms, p90=30ms, p99=92ms
- FusedOps: p50=16ms, p90=23ms, p99=34ms

seq_len=1024, batch=4:
- FlashAttention: p50=48ms, p90=69ms, p99=130ms
- PagedAttention: p50=54ms, p90=95ms, p99=210ms
- FusedOps: p50=44ms, p90=62ms, p99=110ms

seq_len=2048, batch=1 (worst-case single-stream):
- FlashAttention: p50=118ms, p90=145ms, p99=380ms
- PagedAttention: p50=140ms, p90=210ms, p99=480ms
- FusedOps: p50=98ms, p90=125ms, p99=210ms

Notes on numbers: averages and percentiles are steady across runs except p99 which jumps when device memory pressure or small host-side stalls occur. FusedOps shows best p99 in single-stream long-seq tests likely due to fewer kernel handoffs and contiguous memory usage.

Root-cause hypotheses (ranked):
1) Memory allocation and fragmentation leading to internal allocator slow paths and occasional GPU page faults: when model KV cache grows and shrinks across requests we sometimes hit the CUDA allocator slow path or attempt to allocate pinned host memory for async copies.
2) Kernel fusion decisions and autograd graph impacts: fused kernels avoid multiple launches and memcpy but increase register / shared memory pressure; autotuner occasionally picks a configuration with worse latency for high sequence lengths and then later reverts (variance during warmup).
3) Host-side scheduling and GC: our Python harness triggers small GC cycles under some conditions (large number of short-lived tensors), resulting in brief stalls visible at p99.
4) Device-side prefetch/paged attention races: paged-attention relies on GPU prefetching; on heavy memory contention prefetches will be serialized or reissued, producing spikes.

Evidence summary (what we saw in traces):
- NVTX brackets show occasional 50-200ms gaps between nvtx:start and nvtx:end for a single attention forward; inside the gap there are either long kernel launches (single line in Nsight) or multiple short kernels separated by small host synchronization points.
- Nsight system shows memcpy H2D operations interleaving with kernels at the time of the spike: suggests a host->device copy triggered mid-inference (likely for new KV allocation or prefetch).
- Torch profiler attribution shows top CUDA time in: fused_kernel_xxx (when fused), flash_attn_kernel (when flash), and cudaMemcpyAsync calls appear in the timeline around the spike windows.
- CPU-side flame shows brief Python-scheduler bursts (GC or thread wakeups) aligning with some p99 events.

Quick reproducible experiment to isolate allocator:
- Re-run inference with environment:
    PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128
  and prewarm by allocating KV cache to max size before serving. Observe p99 reduction in 3/4 of runs for seq_len>=1024.

Mitigations tested and outcomes:
1) Warm preallocation of KV and caches (preallocate biggest tensor shapes expected): reduced p99 by ~35% for seq>=1024. (Owner: Jinsoo)
2) Force fused ops for single-stream long-seq (config flag): reduced p99 and smoothed variance; small ~5-8% median regression for some mid-batch cases. (Owner: Aisha)
3) Adjust FlashAttention autotuner to avoid certain kernel variants that use >60% shared memory on A100 for seq>1536 — eliminated the very long kernel outliers in our tests. (Owner: Mateo)
4) Set PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF and increase max_split_size_mb: reduced allocator slow-paths and improved consistency. (Owner: Jinsoo)

Operational recommendations (short-term):
- For hosted API route default policy: route seq_len>1536 & batch<=2 to fused ops variant (falls back to flash otherwise). This reduces tail-risk for interactive single-request workloads.
- Enable preallocation for known KV maxima per model at cold start (configurable per-deployment).
- Expose an env var toggle for allocator tuning (PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF) per dedicated instance image and document recommended values.
- Add NVTX instrumentation across attention entry/exit and copying code paths in serving runtime to make future traces easier to correlate.

Longer-term work and experiments (backlog):
- Investigate async prefetch queuing in paged-attention to ensure it never races with critical path kernel launches; consider deterministic prefetch scheduling. (Jinsoo / 2 sprints)
- Kernel autotuner improvements: add a variance-aware penalty in addition to mean-time to avoid rare-but-expensive variants. (Mateo / 3 sprints)
- Memory pool defragmentation heuristics in runtime: introduce background compaction step and measure impact on tail. (SRE + runtime team / 4 sprints)

Immediate next steps (owners + dates):
- Merge temporary fused-ops routing flag into canary branch (Aisha) — ETA 2024-12-06
- Add KV preallocation helper in serving startup (Jinsoo) — ETA 2024-12-10
- Add NVTX markers and update bench harness docs with profiling recipes (Mateo) — ETA 2024-12-08

Open questions / things to watch:
- How do results vary under multi-tenant load and noisy neighbor scenarios (GPU MPS or multiplexing)? We need to replicate with 2-3 active replicas on a single GPU.
- What is the cost impact of always routing to fused ops for high-seq single requests (measured in throughput and GPU-util)? Add cost/latency tradeoff dashboard entry.

Appendix: quick profiling checklist to reproduce spike:
1) Run harness with --seq 2048 --batch 1 --steady-reqs 250/s (or single-shot bursts).
2) Prewarm: run 20 dry-forward passes to materialize caches.
3) Start NSYS capture around the 50th request.
4) Collect torch.profiler snippet for top cuda_time_total entries.
5) Look for cudaMemcpyAsync overlapping kernels and nvtx gaps >100ms.

Notes to reviewers: this doc is intentionally pragmatic and experimental — contains several quick fixes with measurable wins and a small set of more invasive items for the roadmap. Feedback requested on the routing heuristic thresholds and whether we should default preallocation in hosted images.

-- Aisha
